A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MERV work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-question-answering results, architectural ablations, efficiency measurements, and quantitative and qualitative SSv2 analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds the Hiera encoder comparisons in Appendix A.5.1 and Table 11.

M1.justification: The proposed alignment, pooling and projection, cross-attentive fusion, LLaMA-2 backbone, and frozen/full training recipes remain unchanged. Hiera is examined through supplementary encoder-composition ablations within the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training-data mixtures, eight QA benchmarks, and SSv2 open-ended, multiple-choice, and temporal evaluations. The Hiera study uses existing benchmarks and introduces no new task or data domain.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds an explicit Hiera-only VideoLLM comparator alongside ViViT-only, Video-LLaVA, MERV, and Hiera-based MERV variants. v1 mentions considering Hiera but provides no corresponding comparison table. The main Table 1 comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5.1 adds reported evaluation configurations: replacing ViViT with Hiera, adding Hiera as a fifth encoder, and using Hiera alone. Existing training budgets, frame sampling, development/held-out benchmark assignments, and zero-shot evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Hiera ablation tests whether another temporal encoder improves MERV through replacement or addition. Conversely, the class-specific SSv2 analysis shrinks from ten plotted classes in v1 Figure 6 to six in v2 Figure 7. Other ablations and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new Hiera table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results. New Table 11 reports MSVD-QA accuracies of 69.68 for replacing ViViT with Hiera, 69.67 for adding Hiera, and 55.38 for Hiera alone. Four SSv2 class-result groups disappear from the plotted analysis. Table 11's final three column headings conflict with the values and accompanying prose, requiring caution about their benchmark attribution.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 and their mathematical construction remain substantively unchanged. The key-dimension notation changes from d_L to d, consistent with the existing description; no new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its performance framing to comparison with the base model under comparable conditions. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion highlight the 4.62-point TVQA gain instead of the earlier approximately 3.7-point headline; that TVQA result already appears in v1 Table 1. The central contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5.1 newly interprets Hiera's limited benefits through similarity to ViViT and possible temporal-stride sensitivity, suggesting more diverse encoders or additional frames. Appendix A.4.1 also adds interpretation of retained open-ended SSv2 results. Existing resource and encoder-capability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that the Hiera checkpoint underwent MAE pretraining and supervised fine-tuning on Kinetics-400. It also expands the appendix's planned release description to training/evaluation code and all checkpoints. Existing hyperparameters, hardware details, and repository access information are retained; actual availability changes are not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds VTM, VCoder, and Cambrian-1 citations, including a substantive connection between Cambrian-1's spatial alignment and MERV's alignment rationale. Numerous other bibliography changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, clarifies training-recipe explanations, and edits prose throughout while retaining the main section sequence. It adds an appendix contents guide, consolidates appendix organization, moves qualitative examples later, and relocates broader-impact discussion to the main paper.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Figure 2 gains a benchmark radar chart, existing attention examples are redisplayed in the main text, several plots are redrawn, and Table 11 is added. Most qualitative figures are retained but moved and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The Hiera ablation modestly strengthens evidence about the limits of adding encoders, while clearer recipe explanations and appendix organization improve accessibility. The revised performance headline also matches evidence already present in Table 1. These benefits are limited by unchanged core results, fewer displayed SSv2 class results, and the confusing final-column headings in new Table 11.
